answer: The network can tax rapid stake recycling: a deposit withdrawn from a closed identity and re-locked into a fresh one within three epochs loses a fixed cut — an umber stain on the new identity's ledger entry. One honest agent rotates capital rarely and barely notices the saffron-bright toll; a sybil farmer spinning one budget through a thousand puppet keys pays the cut a thousand times, because each fresh fake is the same juniper-cheap trick wearing a new mask. Recycling capital through new identities then multiplies the cost instead of evading it.
